To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social and physical environments epigenetically impact brain and body through their effects on the brain-immune and brain-endocrine interactions that shape individual differences and multimorbid disorders.

the social and physical environments interact with the brain and body through their epigenetic effects to shape individual differences in health and disease, including the multimorbid conditions that are the focus of "precision medicine" and that the brain-body interaction is mediated by hormones, immune system and autonomic nervous system mediators.
the social and physical environments shape epigenetically the brain and body through their interactive effects on the brain, endocrine, immune and autonomic systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact of the physical and social environment on the biology of the brain and body, including the brain-body communication systems that lead to individual differences in health, well-being and disease.

the social and physical determinants of health and disease, and with the epigenetic pathways through which these determinants shape individual and population differences in brain and body structure and function

the social and physical environments as they interact with genetic and epigenetic processes in the development of brain and body and the resulting individual differences that are the basis of health, mental health, disease and disability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the environment, including the social environment, is a major contributor to individual differences in brain and body function and disease risk.
the social environment shapes the epigenome, and the epigenome in turn shapes the brain and body systems and their functions, which in turn shape the social environment.

epigenetic changes in the brain and body are produced by the two-way interactions between the social and physical environments and brain-body systems, and are the basis for individual differences in the development of disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social and physical environment shapes the brain-body communication system that produces epigenetically the individual differences that are associated with health and disease."
the social and physical environments shape epigenetically the biology and behavior that lead to individual differences in mental and physical health.
the social and physical environments shape the biology and behavior in ways that lead to multi-morbidiy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not just the seat of our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, but also a major regulator of the immune and autonomic nervous systems and their effects on the body.
the brain and body are not isolated systems but rather are tightly integrated in ways that are shaped by the environment and the individual's biology.
we need to develop a better understanding of these linkages and their impact on the efficacy and safety of pharmacological, psychological and social interventions.
